title: The Last Queen
tagline: Versailles blazed brightest just before the darkness fell.

scenes.text: Versailles, 1770. The fourteen-year-old Archduchess of Austria becomes Dauphine of France. The Palace of Versailles is the most magnificent building on earth — also the most dangerous. Every marble corridor conceals a rumour; every chandelier illuminates an intrigue.

scenes.speaker: Marie Antoinette
scenes.text: I am to be a queen, and for this I was born. But I did not expect it to be so — complicated.

challenge.instruction: Winter comes to Versailles and the young Dauphine has her sleighs brought out, as at home in Vienna. Steer across the frozen park — a sleigh glides until it hits a bank or a statue — to reach the far landing.
challenge.fact: On 7 May 1770 the fourteen-year-old Archduchess Maria Antonia was handed over to France on an island in the Rhine near Strasbourg, where she left behind her Austrian clothes and attendants. She married the Dauphin, the future Louis XVI, at Versailles on 16 May.

scenes.text: She was young, foreign, and thrust into a court where she was expected to produce heirs, perform magnificence, and never show weakness. The fashions she created swept Europe. The parties she threw became legend. The debt she accumulated became a revolution.

scenes.speaker: Count Axel von Fersen
scenes.text: Your Majesty, the people grow restless. There is talk in Paris — very dangerous talk.

scenes.speaker: Marie Antoinette
scenes.text: There is always talk in Paris. We are the court of France — we do not explain ourselves to pamphleteers.

challenge.instruction: The queen's parties set the fashion, and so does her music: she has brought her old teacher Gluck to Paris. Put the scenes of his Orphée in order for the Opéra.
challenge.fact: Gluck's French operas split Paris in the late 1770s into Gluckists and Piccinnists, partisans of the Italian composer Niccolò Piccinni, and the quarrel was fought out in pamphlets as fiercely as any political cause.

scenes.speaker: Marie Antoinette
scenes.text: I was a queen. I am still a queen. No matter what they do to the crown, they cannot undo what I am.

Her final months in the Temple Prison showed a different woman — stripped of every luxury, she became composed, dignified, and calm. At her trial, when accused of crimes against her son, she appealed to every mother in the courtroom. She was thirty-seven when she died.

challenge.instruction: The royal family's escape plan: help Marie Antoinette navigate the Flight to Varennes.
challenge.fact: In 1791, the royal family disguised themselves and fled toward Austria. They were recognized and captured at Varennes — the king's profile on French coins had been recognized by a local postmaster. The failed flight sealed the monarchy's fate.

challenge.instruction: While the queen waits in the Conciergerie, the Republic that will try her is building a faster France. Raise Chappe's semaphore towers so every city can signal every other with as few towers as possible.
challenge.fact: In the summer of 1793, as Marie Antoinette was moved to the Conciergerie to await trial, the Convention adopted Claude Chappe's semaphore and ordered a line from Paris to Lille. She was guillotined on 16 October 1793; the line opened the next year.

scenes.speaker: Marie Antoinette

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 5 · Face Down. Win two attacks: fight at St Petersburg where the Business War is running, then carry the fight to London by starting your own event there.
challenge.fact: A card on the board can be public (face up) or private (face down). A private card hides its identity and stats from rivals until an attack reveals every card at that location. Your own cards deploy face down; Go Public when being seen helps you.
